simple.meaning: אֵיפֹה (ʼêyphôh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “what place? ; also (of time) when? ; or (of means) how?.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 10 times in Genesis, Judges, Ruth, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, and 3 more, beginning at Genesis 37:16. The surrounding contexts include family, flock, death, Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֵיפֹה (H375) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אֵיפֹה (ʼêyphôh) / H375 is traced through Genesis 37:16, Judges 8:18, Ruth 2:19, 1 Samuel 19:22 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: what place? ; also (of time) when? ; or (of means) how?
definitions.full: H375. ephoh אֵיפֹה (from אַי & מֹּה here ) adverb 1. where? Gen 37:16 ; 1Sam 19:22 ; 2Sam 9:4 ; Isa 49:21 ; Jer 3:2 ; Job 4:7 ; 38:4 ; Ruth 2:19 ; in indirect sentence Jer 36:19 (less common than אַיֵה , used of persons [contrast אֵיוֶֿה ] and with a verb [contrast אַיֵּה ]). 2 of what kind? ( quails ?) only Judg 8:18 .

occurrences.englishText: He said, “I am looking for my brothers. Tell me, please, where they are feeding the flock.”
Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men were they whom you killed at Tabor?”
Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where have you gleaned today? Where have you worked? Blessed be he who noticed you.”
Then he also went to Ramah, and came to the great well that is in Secu: and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?”
The king said to him, “Where is he?”
“Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?
Then you will say in your heart, ‘Who has conceived these for me, since I have been bereaved of my children

“Lift up your eyes to the bare heights, and see! Where have you not been lain with? You have sat waiting for them by the road, as an Arabian in the wilderness. You have polluted the land with your prostitution and with your wickedness.
Then the princes said to Baruch, “You and Jeremiah go hide. Don’t let anyone know where you are.”
